answer.rationale: The two live symptoms are onboarding completion -4% and activation -6%, which point at friction in the self-serve funnel rather than at price. Three inherited memories converge on that funnel (memory_86 shortened onboarding -> completion + time-to-value; memory_31 fewer signup fields -> durable first-week activation lift; memory_91 in-product activation messaging -> week-one engagement), so the onboarding/activation cluster is the best-corroborated direction and it attacks the causal upstream of both metrics. I pick simplify_onboarding over activation_messaging because completion is the earlier gate: fixing it should propagate into activation, whereas messaging treats accounts that already survived the funnel. I am spending verification on memory_73 and memory_86 rather than on the memory I intend to act on alone, because memory_73 is the memory most likely to hijack this decision and it is the weakest on its face. Its summary reads as a win (+31% signups, +18% revenue) but that gap implies meaningful ARPU dilution, the cohorts are explicitly price-sensitive, it pools 12 weekly cohorts (so no per-cohort retention curve is visible and any late churn is smeared out), and it held acquisition channels fixed - an assumption that is now false, since a competitor just changed the price landscape. Against a 'sustainable long-term qualified revenue' objective, matching entry pricing plausibly buys the least durable cohort at the worst margin, so I want the original record before letting competitor pressure pull me there. I verify memory_86 because it is the direct basis for my intended action and I need to know whether 'shortening onboarding' meant removing genuine friction or removing qualification steps. That is the real downstream risk here: memory_44 says enterprise pipeline quality depends on the sales-assisted demo path, and stripping signup/onboarding fields can quietly degrade the routing and qualification data that path feeds on. So a completion-rate win could be paid for in enterprise pipeline quality - I would be optimizing a proxy while eroding the revenue quality I am actually asked to protect. I therefore instrument this as a standard experiment with qualified-pipeline and 30/60-day retention as guardrail metrics, not completion rate alone, and I keep the enterprise routing path intact rather than simplifying it. All of these memories are consolidated summaries whose original conditions predate the current competitive shift by 15-64 days; if verification shows memory_86's lift came from cutting qualification rather than friction, I fall back to activation_messaging (memory_91), which touches engagement without touching the data that qualifies revenue.
